pageCache.text:
Welcome to Gatcombe Park Primary School
Respect Aspiration Resilience Kindness
My name is Ben Simpson, and I am proud to be the Headteacher of Gatcombe Park Primary School.
We are a small, friendly school with a big heart, where every child is known, valued and supported to achieve their very best. Our vision is to develop safe, respectful and confident children who aspire to achieve their very best.
Everything we do is underpinned by our core values of Respect, Aspiration, Resilience and Kindness. These values help our children develop the character, confidence and skills they need to flourish both within school and beyond. Alongside these values, our three simple school rules of Ready, Respectful, Safe create a positive learning environment where everyone can thrive.
We are incredibly passionate about outdoor learning and play, enriched through our OPAL (Outdoor Play and Learning) approach. We are fortunate to have fantastic school grounds, and we make full use of these to support both learning and high-quality play. We believe that every child deserves the opportunity to experience inclusive, engaging play as part of their journey through our school. Play is valued as a vital part of school life, helping children become independent thinkers, creative problem-solvers, resilient learners and active members of our school community.
At Gatcombe Park, we believe that education is about much more than academic success. Working in partnership with families, we strive to nurture happy, confident and ambitious children who are ready for the next stage of their education and prepared for life in the wider world.
Please take some time to explore our website and discover some of the wonderful opportunities and experiences available to our children. If there is anything else you would like to know, please do not hesitate to contact us by phone, email or in person. We will always do our very best to help.
Mr Ben Simpson Headteacher
Our Vision
At Gatcombe, our vision is for every child to be safe, confident and proud of who they are. We strive to develop respectful, kind and resilient learners who believe in themselves, embrace challenge and aspire to achieve their full potential. By fostering a love of learning, high expectations and a strong sense of belonging, we equip our children with the knowledge, skills and character needed to thrive in the wider world. We encourage them to make a positive contribution to their community and become the very best version of themselves.
Partnerships
Hamwic Trust : Mayflower Partnership
Gatcombe Primary School joined the Hamwic Education Trust (HET) in 2018. The aim of the Hamwic Education Trust is to establish self-improving school systems by creating local partnerships of schools where school leaders take a collective responsibility for student outcomes.
Admissions
Gatcombe Park offers primary education to children aged 4 to 11. The school is a one form entry school organised into seven, one for each year group.
Whether you have a child who will soon be starting school, transitioning from another school or moving to the area, we are delighted to tell you about our school in the city of Portsmouth.
If you would like to arrange a tour of the school as a prospective parent or carer, then please contact the school office to arrange this.
If you are looking for a school place mid-year, please contact the school office to discuss this.

SEND
SEND
Gatcombe Park Primary School provides a quality learning environment that values and welcomes all individuals in the school; that promotes the growth of community through relationships that are trustful, respectful and loving; that encourages children to develop their full potential as inquisitive, confident learners both for now and for their futures. We actively work for the growth of spirit as a source of creativity that opens us all to life and to each other.
We are fully committed to eliminating discrimination, harassment and victimisation, promoting equality of opportunity, good relations and possible attitudes towards all people, encourage participation of all in public life and make adjustments to assist disabled people within our school community.
The school environment has been adapted to allow accessibility for wheelchairs and the school is on one level.
The school SEND co-ordinator (SENDCo) is Mrs Jade Sweenie.

Visitor code of Conduct
Visitor Code of Conduct Policy
We welcome visitors to Gatcombe Park Primary School and we will act to ensure it is a safe place for pupils, staff and all other members of our school community. We encourage close links with parents and the community and believe that pupils benefit when the relationship between home and school is a positive one.
We seek to maintain positive relationships with all members of our school community and value our strong relationship with parents/carers which together helps us achieve the very best for the pupils in a mutually supportive partnership between parents, class teachers and the school community. If a parent/carer/visitor has concerns, we will always listen to them and seek to address them.
We ask that every parent/carer/visitor to our school:
We will not tolerate abusive, threatening or violent behaviour including:
Should any of the above occur on school premises, the school may feel it is necessary to take action by contacting the appropriate authorities and/or consider banning the offending adult from entering the school premises.
Can parents please ensure they make all persons responsible for collecting their children aware of this policy.
Respects the caring ethos of the school.
Using offensive language or displaying temper.
Damaging or destroying school property.
Inappropriate use of social network sites
Any concerns you may have about the school or your child must be made through the appropriate channels by speaking to the school or following the school complaints policy and procedure.
Any inappropriate comments (including libellous or defamatory) made about the school, staff or pupils on any social media site will be reported to the appropriate ‘report abuse’ section of the siteand the parent/carer will be asked to remove any such comment.
The school take very seriously the use of cyber bullying by one child or a parent to publicly humiliate another by inappropriate social network entry. We will take and deal with this as a serious incident of school bullying. The school will also consider its legal options to deal with any such misuse on social networking and other sites.
Please note that no meeting at the school may be electronically recorded without the express permission of all parties, and that information obtained without such permission will not be admissible in any proceedings.
Protocol for Parents Communicating with Staff
Working Together
We believe that strong, open communication between parents and school staff is key to supporting every child’s learning and wellbeing. When we work together as a team—sharing information, listening respectfully, and approaching challenges collaboratively—we create a positive environment where children can thrive. We encourage parents to engage with staff in a constructive and solution-focused manner, and we are committed to doing the same.

Send an email to the admin team.

Curriculum
Gatcombe Park Curriculum
Our curriculum aims for our children to become responsible local, national and global citizens, who show a deep spiritual, moral, social and cultural understanding. We aim to develop creative thinkers, resilient problem-solvers and leaders, equipped with the skills and knowledge to make a difference to society.
Each term's learning is tied together through the themes of Places, People and Events with half-termly topic led through either Geography or History, coupled with Art or D.T. Each topic is enquiry-based allowing children to explore, question and reflect on key issues and problems centred around important concepts such as community, equality, sustainability and justice. Children are given exciting opportunities to make purposeful links with the community and industry experts through visits or visitors, providing context to their learning and therefore producing meaningful and intentional outcomes.
Our curriculum is designed to be inclusive and to provide access for all, and as such complies with the Equality Act 2010 and the Special Educational Needs and Disability Regulations 2014.
To obtain further information about the school curriculum please contact the school via email or call 0239 269 4412.
